subject.title: [Bug] Zombie worker processes spawned by process supervisor on unexpected SIGKILL

question: Should OpenClaw guarantee termination of supervisor-created workers after an uncatchable parent SIGKILL, and if so which supported platforms and worker classes are in scope?
rationale: SIGKILL bypasses normal shutdown, while the proposed parent-death and startup-reaping approaches have materially different portability and false-positive tradeoffs that source inspection alone cannot safely choose.

options.title: Request focused reproduction first
options.body: Keep the report open and require a current Linux process-tree reproduction that identifies the exact spawned worker path before selecting a lifecycle contract.

options.title: Adopt Linux-only parent-death handling
options.body: Define a supported Linux worker-launch contract with explicit non-Linux behavior and targeted tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep current shutdown-only contract
options.body: Document that abrupt process death is delegated to the service manager or container cgroup rather than daemon startup cleanup.

recommendation.title: Request focused reproduction first
recommendation.body: Keep the report open and require a current Linux process-tree reproduction that identifies the exact spawned worker path before selecting a lifecycle contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The affected implementation paths are identified in the report, but repository history could not be inspected to name an individual owner.
